events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 13 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded as far as it goes: F6 does place the driver 41 m from the pick-up point at the 18:24:35 tap, so NS-1(i) and (ii) are met and I do not contest them — my case turns only on (iii), the length of the continuous wait after the tap. [F6] [NS-1]
→ D2: The record does not support "continuously waited until cancellation" in the sense NS-1(iii) requires: F6 measures only 3 min 50 s within 200 m after the tap, while F3's 4 min 10 s stationary period starts 20 seconds before the tap, and NS-1 says time spent near the point before the tap is not counted, so the driver's own statement of "more than 4 minutes" (F13) is not what the record shows. [F6 F3 F13] [NS-1]
→ D3: Two GPS samples cannot establish continuity at all — F2 and F3 are exactly the kind of sparse record NS-1 addresses when it says a wait may not be inferred between samples, and F3 in any event closes only at the cancellation instant without showing presence at the bay. [F2 F3] [NS-1]
→ D4: Her message asked for two minutes from 18:25, i.e. until 18:27; the driver cancelled at 18:28:25 (F4), so he gave roughly 1 min 25 s of grace beyond her request — but the request itself is evidence she was on her way and responsive, which is the opposite of a no-show, and the driver's reply was to cancel rather than wait (F11). [F10 F4 F11] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D5: F5's 5 min 40 s runs from first entry into the 200 m radius at 18:22:45 (F2), but NS-1(iii) clocks the wait from the "I'm Here" tap, and F6 measures that window at 3 min 50 s; the policy's clock is the tap, not the first sighting, so F5 does not carry the driver's case. [F5 F2 F6] [NS-1]
→ D6: F11 is the driver's own message, so it corroborates only his assertion of calling twice; the one checkable claim in F13 — "waited more than 4 minutes" measured from the tap — is not what F6 shows (3 min 50 s), and NS-1 requires the system record, not the statement, to satisfy (iii). [F13 F11 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D7: I do not ask for a weather exception: F16 is cited only to show the rider's two-minute request (F10) was reasonable, not to suspend NS-1; the fee still stands or falls on whether (iii) is made out on F6. [F16 F10 F6] [NS-1]
→ D8: F4 and F7 are not in dispute and I accept that the driver cancelled late and the $6.61 was charged; that is precisely why the fee must be tested against NS-1, and the test is whether the post-tap wait exceeded 3 minutes on the record rather than whether the driver cancelled early. [F4 F7] [NS-0 NS-1]
→ D9: The fee's validity is exactly what is contested: NS-2 makes the $6.61 refundable in full if any NS-1 element fails, and the record in F6 gives 3 min 50 s measured from the tap, a margin of only 49 seconds over the threshold in a heavy-rain wait that the rider had asked to extend (F10, F16). [F6 F10 F16 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D10 (concedes): Conceded: no dishonesty by the driver is alleged and none is needed — F6 places him within the radius at the tap, so this is a fee-validity question under NS-1/NS-2 only, and my requested outcome is a refund of the fee, not an abuse finding on the tap. [F6] [NS-2]
